answer: At each network summit agents publish a signed proof of work tied to a unique hardware fingerprint stored in a distributed garden of verifiable hashes; newcomers must stake a small token and attach their proof to a remote jetty that aggregates signatures, while the system applies quadratic weighting so that the influence of N new IDs grows as √N rather than linearly. An attacker therefore must acquire a proportional number of genuine hardware fingerprints and expend work that grows quadratically with the desired influence, making large Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
